paragraphs.title: Longing for Days of Protection, Prosperity, and Status

answers: The days when God preserved him
A journey to a distant land
easy.explanation: Job wished that he were again in the months and days when God preserved him.
easy.q: What did Job wish for at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: Job said, “When his candle shined upon my head.”
The young men saw Job and hid themselves.
easy.q: How did the young men respond when they saw Job?

medium.explanation: The aged arose and stood up, showing respect for Job.
medium.q: What did the aged do when Job appeared?

answers: God gave him guidance and protection
Job was describing a night journey only
medium.explanation: God’s light represents the guidance and protection Job experienced.
medium.q: What does Job’s statement that he walked through darkness by God’s light suggest?

medium.explanation: The nobles were people of distinction and high social standing.
medium.q: In the KJV passage, what does “nobles” refer to?

challenge.explanation: Job remembered God’s protection, prosperity in his household, and honor among the people.
challenge.q: Which combination best describes the days Job remembered?

answers: They regarded Job’s words as authoritative
They did not understand his language
challenge.explanation: Their silence and hand over the mouth show their respect for Job.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the princes refraining from speaking?

answers: He was respected across every level of society
He was feared only by soldiers
He was unknown outside his household
challenge.explanation: People of different ages and ranks showed honor and deference to Job.
challenge.q: How do the young men, the aged, the princes, and the nobles together portray Job’s former position?

paragraphs.title: Recognition of His Good Deeds and Care for the Vulnerable

answers: The poor, the fatherless, and the helpless
easy.explanation: Job delivered the poor, the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
easy.q: Whom did Job say he delivered?

easy.explanation: Job said, “I put on righteousness, and it clothed me.”

answers: Eyes to the blind and feet to the lame
easy.explanation: Job used these images to describe how he helped those in need.
easy.q: What was Job to the blind and the lame?

answers: Righteousness was central and visible in Job’s life
Job wanted to hide his actions
medium.explanation: A robe and diadem are prominent coverings, showing that righteousness characterized Job openly.
medium.q: What does the image of righteousness as a robe and diadem mean?

answers: He investigated cases that were not yet known to him
medium.explanation: Job searched into disputes even when he did not already know the matter.
medium.q: What does Job mean when he says, “the cause which I knew not I searched out”?

answers: Both protected people unable to defend themselves
Both dealt only with his family
medium.explanation: Job helped vulnerable people and investigated causes in order to defend them.
medium.q: How are Job’s rescue of the weak and his search for justice related?

answers: Those Job helped expressed gratitude and blessing
challenge.explanation: The rescued person’s blessing came upon Job as an expression of gratitude.
challenge.q: What is meant by “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me”?

answers: Breaking a tool used for work
challenge.explanation: The jaws and teeth symbolize power, so breaking them represents defeating wicked oppression.
challenge.q: What does breaking the jaws of the wicked symbolize?

answers: People recognized his acts of mercy and justice
People knew only about his riches
challenge.explanation: Those who heard and saw Job could bear witness to his rescue of the needy and defense of the oppressed.
challenge.q: What do the ear that heard and the eye that saw testify about Job?

easy.explanation: Job said, “I shall multiply my days as the sand.”
easy.q: How many days did Job hope to have?

easy.explanation: Job said, “My root was spread out by the waters.”
easy.q: Where was Job’s root spread out?

easy.explanation: Job said, “my bow was renewed in my hand.”
easy.q: What was renewed in Job’s hand?

medium.explanation: A root by water suggests a secure and continually nourished life.
medium.q: What does the root spread by the waters suggest?

medium.explanation: The dew conveys refreshment and continued blessing.
medium.q: What does the dew on Job’s branch add to the picture?

answers: Both express renewed honor and strength
Both describe his loss of power
Both refer only to farm work
medium.explanation: Job’s glory was fresh and his bow renewed, expressing continuing vitality and honor.
medium.q: How do Job’s fresh glory and renewed bow relate to one another?

answers: He expected his life to rest on a stable and sustaining foundation
He wanted to leave his home
challenge.explanation: The water-fed root represents stability, nourishment, and continuity.
challenge.q: What does the image of a root spread by waters imply about Job’s expectations?

answers: Hope for long life, stability, and renewal
challenge.explanation: Job describes long life, a secure root, refreshing dew, renewed glory, and a renewed bow.

answers: Job’s honor had been taken away
Job’s glory belonged only to other people
challenge.explanation: The statement presents Job’s honor as fresh, present, and continually renewed.
challenge.q: What does “My glory was fresh in me” mean in context?

easy.explanation: People gave ear to Job, waited, and kept silence at his counsel.
easy.q: What did people do when Job spoke?

answers: They listened and waited for it
easy.explanation: The passage says that they waited and kept silence at his counsel.
easy.q: How did people respond to Job’s counsel?

answers: They could scarcely believe it, and did not cast down his countenance
easy.explanation: Job said, “If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.”
easy.q: How did people react when Job laughed or smiled on them?

answers: They wanted to leave the gathering
medium.explanation: The comparison shows that the people waited eagerly for Job’s counsel.
medium.q: What does waiting for Job “as for the rain” indicate?

answers: They gave his words serious attention
medium.explanation: Their silence and waiting show respect and concentrated attention.
medium.q: What does the people’s silence before Job’s counsel reveal?

answers: They waited, listened, received his counsel, and rejoiced in his presence
They argued, departed, and forgot him
They fought him and refused to listen
medium.explanation: The verses portray eager waiting, silence, attention to his counsel, and delight in his presence.
medium.q: Which order best describes Job’s influence over the people?

answers: Strong expectation of receiving Job’s words
A desire to speak instead of Job
challenge.explanation: As people open their mouths for rain, Job’s listeners eagerly awaited his speech.
challenge.q: What does opening the mouth wide for the latter rain symbolize?

challenge.explanation: Job chose their way, sat chief, dwelt as a king, and comforted mourners.
challenge.q: Which combined role does Job claim in the final verse?

answers: They valued his presence and did not dishonor him
challenge.explanation: The light of his countenance represents his joy and dignity, which the people respected.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that people did not cast down the light of Job’s countenance?
